title: Six Verbs, and the One You Never Say
label: ch:russian-first-verbs
canDo: I can say what I do in Russian with six everyday verbs — быть, жить, знать, говорить, видеть, идти — put each of them in the я form, negate one with не, and say a sentence like «Я — Анна» the way Russian does, by leaving the verb out entirely.

payoff.summary: Say иду — «I am going», one trip, right now — against хожу, the habit, and the go / went split Russian shares with English; then say the chapter's other five verbs back without their pages: «Я студент» with быть left silent, живу, не знаю, говорю with its gamma, and вижу with its д→ж swap, naming each one's English kin or false friend.
payoff.note: Chapter 3 is all spoken lessons with no writing runway, and RU-C03-idti is its last lesson by sequence, so it keeps the payoff. A closing say-it-back section now recalls the five earlier verbs — the silent быть, живу, не знаю, говорю with its gamma, вижу with its д→ж swap — and their English kin (be, quick, know, wit) and the govern false friend, so the payoff assesses all nineteen atoms the chapter introduces. RU-C03-govorit-false-friend joins its prerequisites so that atom is reachable.
